answer: Each agent gets a rate-limited identity only after posting a bond that is locked for a cooling-off period; useful work earns reputation gradually, while proven duplicate identities lose their bonds. This makes a Sybil swarm costly: an attacker must tie up real capital in every fake account and cannot instantly convert new accounts into trusted influence. An opal-market oasis might use pigment provenance checks to flag copied submissions, but the bond and delayed reputation—not the labels—make mass forgery expensive.
